alternatives.reason: I considered attaching the fibres first, but fitting their channels addresses the other current goal.

reaction: It was surprising that the change travels without one ion going the whole length.

expectation: I expect the channel-bearing fibres to attach to the nerve cells with receiving branches.

effect: The branches, bodies and fibres now form continuous nerve cells; their endings release chemical messengers to the next cell.

reason: This is the only offered combination, and the vessels can bring oxygen and food to the nerve cells.

reaction: The finished tissue brings the signal pathway and its blood supply together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the channels was most worthwhile: the picture explained how an electrical change travels along a fibre through local ion movements.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the receiving branches was predictable, although the arrows made their job clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the electrical change travels without a single ion going the whole length of the fibre.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the goals and pictures gave each a purpose. The final vessel pairing was also the only offered combination.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because seeing the electrical change pass along a fibre and the chemical messenger at its ending made me curious about what happens next.
